items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We left Bernard Ighner’s version intact.

ctx.x: But if I had went back and said, let me study the original, it would have changed my whole opinion, my whole approach to the song. I tried not to do that, to keep me from imitating the original, and leaving the original intact, so that it can still be the classic that it is. That’s exactly what happened. We left Bernard Ighner’s version intact. Ours is different, and so is Randy’s. I’m happy for that.
Then after Weekend in L.A., now you got to follow up This Masquerade, On Broadway. What was – was there pressure on you now at this point? It’s like, “Okay, George, what you going to do now?”
